results.notes: SA earnings summary says EPS beat consensus by $0.13 and revenue beat by $4.06B. Data-center revenue was $89B, +18% QoQ; hyperscale was $49B, +13% sequentially; ACIE was $40B, +25% sequentially and +138% Y/Y.

NVDA.guidance: Next-qtr revenue: $108B +/- 2%; GM guide: Q3 FY27 GAAP and non-GAAP 74% +/- 50 bps; expected Q4 trough 71%-72%; FY28 expected 72%-73%; Annual / LT: Preliminary FY28 revenue growth approximately 70% Y/Y; supply expected to remain a bottleneck through at least FY28; Guide vs consensus: unknown

guidanceDetail.grossMargin: Q3 FY27 GAAP and non-GAAP 74% +/- 50 bps; expected Q4 trough 71%-72%; FY28 expected 72%-73%
guidanceDetail.annual: Preliminary FY28 revenue growth approximately 70% Y/Y; supply expected to remain a bottleneck through at least FY28

positives.text: Record Q2 revenue of $96.22B more than doubled year-over-year; SA summary reports 105.85% Y/Y growth and an EPS/revenue beat.
Data-center revenue reached $89B, up 18% sequentially; ACIE revenue was $40B, up 25% sequentially and 138% Y/Y.
AWS is deploying an additional 2 million NVIDIA GPUs from Q2 FY27 through Q2 FY29; Vera Rubin production shipments commenced and are expected to be the fastest product ramp in company history.
NVIDIA expects approximately 70% FY28 revenue growth; demand is described as higher, but the outlook is supply constrained.
Vera CPU revenue is preliminarily expected to more than double in FY28; management sees approximately $20B total server-CPU demand.

negatives.text: Memory pricing is rising sharply; management reset Q3 gross-margin expectations to 74% and expects a Q4 bottom at 71%-72%.
Current Hopper shipments are dilutive to corporate gross margin, and the forward outlook contains no China data-center compute revenue due to geopolitical uncertainty.
GAAP and non-GAAP operating expenses rose 10% and 11% sequentially; full-year FY27 OpEx is expected to grow in the low 50s.
Inventory rose to $32B and days sales outstanding to 60 days, reflecting preparation for Vera Rubin and extended payment terms on large customer purchases.

uncertainties.text: Supply is expected to remain a bottleneck through at least FY28, despite demand that management says is materially above the 70% outlook.
NVIDIA has invested nearly $50B in frontier AI labs and may provide selective credit enhancement; management notes the scale and circular-financing criticism.
AI-lab demand supported by NVIDIA balance-sheet leverage could represent roughly one-quarter of next year's business; customer payment terms have lengthened.

NVDA.commentary: AI demand: Demand is broadening across hyperscalers, AI labs, neoclouds, enterprises and sovereigns; AI agents require materially more compute than conventional use cases. | Capacity: Neocloud partners are expected to exit the year with 8GW of installed capacity versus approximately 3GW at end-2025; Vera Rubin is expected to be about 20% of Q3 data-center revenue. | Gross margin: Memory scarcity is driven by the AI buildout; price increases are expected to be offset over time by executed customer price increases, but management expects margins to bottom in Q4. | Customers: AWS expansion, OpenAI commitments of approximately 12GW through 2030, and additional frontier-lab demand support future shipments, while China is excluded from forward data-center compute outlook.

commentaryDetail.text: Demand is broadening across hyperscalers, AI labs, neoclouds, enterprises and sovereigns; AI agents require materially more compute than conventional use cases.
Neocloud partners are expected to exit the year with 8GW of installed capacity versus approximately 3GW at end-2025; Vera Rubin is expected to be about 20% of Q3 data-center revenue.
Memory scarcity is driven by the AI buildout; price increases are expected to be offset over time by executed customer price increases, but management expects margins to bottom in Q4.
AWS expansion, OpenAI commitments of approximately 12GW through 2030, and additional frontier-lab demand support future shipments, while China is excluded from forward data-center compute outlook.

qa.question: Why guide to about 70% FY28 revenue growth when management says demand is higher?
qa.answer: Management says supply, not demand, supports the 70% outlook; supply is expected to remain a bottleneck through FY28.

qa.question: What is the near-term gross-margin path?
qa.answer: Q3 GAAP and non-GAAP gross margin is guided to 74% +/- 50 bps; management expects Q4 at 71%-72% and FY28 at 72%-73%.

qa.question: How material are frontier AI labs to future revenue and risk?
qa.answer: Demand from labs for which NVIDIA may leverage its balance sheet could be roughly one-quarter of next year's business; NVIDIA has invested nearly $50B and may provide selective credit enhancement.

qa.question: What customer capacity is already visible?
qa.answer: AWS plans an additional 2M GPUs from this quarter through Q2 FY29; OpenAI's existing and planned commitments represent approximately 12GW of NVIDIA compute through 2030.

qa.question: What is driving the mix beyond GPUs?
qa.answer: Management expects Vera CPU revenue to more than double in FY28, with approximately $20B of total server-CPU demand; networking revenue also grew 18% sequentially in Q2.

positives.text: Record Q3 revenue of $29.6B grew 86% Y/Y; operating income grew 92% Y/Y and operating margin reached a record 67.9%.
AI semiconductor revenue reached $16.7B, up 221% Y/Y and 54% sequentially; Q4 AI revenue is guided to $21.7B, up 236% Y/Y.
Management expects FY26 AI revenue of approximately $58B, FY27 AI revenue of approximately $115B, and FY28 AI semiconductor revenue of approximately $230B.
Google agreement contemplates multi-tens of billions of dollars of TPUs annually over the next several years; Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta deployments provide multi-year XPU visibility.
Q3 free cash flow was a record $13.7B, or 46% of revenue; management expects substantial operating leverage despite mix pressure.

negatives.text: Consolidated gross margin was 75%, down 210 bps sequentially as AI semiconductor revenue became a larger mix; Q4 is guided to approximately 73% versus 78% a year ago.
Increasing XPU memory content is diluting consolidated gross margin; management guides one quarter at a time for future margins.
Non-AI semiconductor revenue was $4.2B, flat sequentially; wireless declined within the non-AI mix.
Q4 CapEx is expected to be $1.4B as Broadcom invests in semiconductor capacity; deployment timing depends on land, power and data-center shells.

uncertainties.text: Broadcom says demand exceeds the $115B FY27 and $230B FY28 AI outlooks, but supply and timely deployment of customer data centers constrain what can be shipped.
The AI XPV platform uses third-party financing for Anthropic and OpenAI; future residual-value guarantees are deal-specific and no new maximum exposure was disclosed.
Long-term XPU revenue depends on frontier-lab customer choices, land/power/shell readiness and continued supply of leading-edge wafers, substrates and HBM.

AVGO.commentary: AI demand: Six XPU customers are accelerating custom-accelerator adoption; Q4 XPUs and AI networking are each expected to triple Y/Y. | Customers: Anthropic is expected to deploy 1GW of Ironwood in 2026, another 5GW in 2027 and 10GW in 2028; OpenAI is planned for 1.3GW in 2027 and over 5GW in 2028; Meta has line of sight to 3GW through 2028. | Networking: Tomahawk 6 is deployed across AI hyperscalers and Tomahawk Ultra is beginning scale-up deployments in Q3 and FY27; AI networking revenue is expected to grow as fast as XPU revenue over the next few years. | Gross margin: Mix is shifting toward XPUs with higher memory content, but management expects operating leverage to preserve approximately 66% Q4 operating margin even as gross margin declines.

commentaryDetail.text: Six XPU customers are accelerating custom-accelerator adoption; Q4 XPUs and AI networking are each expected to triple Y/Y.
Anthropic is expected to deploy 1GW of Ironwood in 2026, another 5GW in 2027 and 10GW in 2028; OpenAI is planned for 1.3GW in 2027 and over 5GW in 2028; Meta has line of sight to 3GW through 2028.

Tomahawk 6 is deployed across AI hyperscalers and Tomahawk Ultra is beginning scale-up deployments in Q3 and FY27; AI networking revenue is expected to grow as fast as XPU revenue over the next few years.
Mix is shifting toward XPUs with higher memory content, but management expects operating leverage to preserve approximately 66% Q4 operating margin even as gross margin declines.

qa.question: Why should investors believe the $115B FY27 and $230B FY28 AI outlooks?
qa.answer: Broadcom says demand is higher than the outlooks and supply has been secured for those targets, but actual shipment timing also depends on data-center deployment readiness.

qa.question: What is the gross-margin risk from XPU mix?
qa.answer: Consolidated Q3 gross margin was 75%, down 210 bps sequentially; Q4 is guided to approximately 73% as XPU memory content rises, while operating margin is guided to approximately 66%.

qa.question: What financing risk is associated with Anthropic and OpenAI?
qa.answer: Broadcom established an XPV platform with third-party capital; future residual-value guarantees will be evaluated deal by deal, and management disclosed no new maximum exposure.

qa.question: How visible is customer-specific XPU demand?
qa.answer: Anthropic has a stated 1GW/5GW/10GW path across 2026-2028; OpenAI is planned at 1.3GW in 2027 and over 5GW in 2028; Meta has line of sight to 3GW through 2028.

qa.question: Can operating income grow despite lower gross margin?
qa.answer: Management expects strong operating leverage: Q4 operating margin is guided to approximately 66%, flat Y/Y, despite Q4 gross margin guidance of approximately 73%.
